title.bn: জাভায় স্ট্রিং আর লেখা তৈরির বিল্ডার

summary.en: Compare string content, work with UTF-16 indices and build text without changing immutable strings.
summary.bn: String-এর মান তুলনা করো, ইনডেক্স বোঝো আর StringBuilder দিয়ে লেখা গড়ো।

notes: StringBuilder is available since Java 5; the methods shown need no newer feature than Java 17.

sections.title: Text is an object with rules
Follow returned text and mutable builders
Use a builder for repeated appends
Choose immutable text or a mutable construction buffer

examples.title: A method result must be saved
examples.explanationHtml: Ignoring the returned uppercase text leaves code equal to cse. Assigning the result changes the reference to CSE.

examples.title: Identity and content
examples.explanationHtml: new creates a separate String object. The references differ, but the character content matches.

examples.title: Extract a course number
examples.explanationHtml: The seven UTF-16 units include the space. substring starts at index 4 and charAt(0) returns C.

examples.title: Build a roll list
examples.explanationHtml: The builder grows one piece at a time and places commas only between rolls.

practice.title: Course code length
practice.statementHtml: Input: one nonempty ASCII course token without spaces. Print its length.

practice.title: Same password text
practice.statementHtml: Input: two nonempty ASCII tokens. Print Same if their content is equal; otherwise print Different.

practice.title: Reverse a short code
practice.statementHtml: Input: one ASCII token of length 1 to 30. Build its reverse with StringBuilder and print it.
hints: Walk backwards from length minus one.

practice.title: Comma-separated rolls
practice.statementHtml: Input: n from 0 to 20. Print rolls 1 through n separated by comma-space, or Empty for zero.
hints: Append the separator before every roll except the first.

quiz.prompt: Does substring replace the source string when its result is ignored?
quiz.explanation: The original String is immutable. Ignoring substring leaves s pointing to CSE212.

quiz.prompt: Do separate String objects with equal characters pass both comparisons?
quiz.explanation: The separate references compare false with ==; equals compares their matching content.

quiz.prompt: How does StringBuilder append an int after text?
quiz.explanation: Each append adds a textual representation, so the builder becomes R23.

quiz.prompt: Which call gives the first code unit of text?
quiz.explanation: String uses methods rather than array indexing syntax.

quiz.prompt: Which String method checks a prefix?
quiz.explanation: startsWith checks whether the initial content matches another string.

quiz.prompt: What is the end index rule for substring(begin, end)?
options: begin is included and end is excluded
quiz.explanation: The half-open range makes the length equal to end minus begin.

quiz.prompt: What does a String variable assignment copy?
options: A reference to a String object
quiz.explanation: The reference is copied. Shared String content is safe because the object cannot be mutated.

quiz.prompt: Why can == seem to work for some string literals?
options: Every string has one possible object
quiz.explanation: Literal interning can make references equal, but text comparison should still use equals.

quiz.prompt: Which type suits repeated appends inside a text-building loop?
quiz.explanation: A builder keeps a mutable character buffer instead of requesting repeated immutable string results.

quiz.prompt: Can length() always count user-perceived characters accurately?
options: Yes; all characters use one char
No; it counts UTF-16 code units
quiz.explanation: Supplementary characters use two code units, and combined visible characters may use several.

quiz.prompt: Why use Locale.ROOT when uppercasing a machine-readable course code?
options: To avoid dependence on the default language locale
quiz.explanation: Case conversion can be locale-sensitive; a fixed policy makes code normalization predictable.

keyPoints.en: String objects cannot change their characters after creation.
keyPoints.bn: String বানানোর পরে তার ভেতরের অক্ষর বদলায় না।

keyPoints.en: String methods often return a new result instead of changing the receiver.
keyPoints.bn: String-এর মেথড সাধারণত মূল মান না বদলে নতুন ফল দেয়।

keyPoints.en: equals compares string content while == compares references.
keyPoints.bn: equals লেখার মান মেলায়, আর == রেফারেন্স মেলায়।

keyPoints.en: String indices count UTF-16 code units.
keyPoints.bn: String-এর ইনডেক্স UTF-16 কোড ইউনিট গোনে।

keyPoints.en: StringBuilder appends text to a mutable buffer.
keyPoints.bn: StringBuilder-এর পরিবর্তনযোগ্য বাফারে লেখা যোগ করা যায়।

examQuestions.question: Distinguish String immutability from reassigning a String variable.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The object characters cannot change. The variable may be assigned a reference to another String. A final String variable prevents that reassignment too.

examQuestions.question: Explain why new String("Lab").equals("Lab") is true while reference equality need not be true.
examQuestions.answerHtml: equals compares character content. new creates a distinct object, so identity differs even when the content matches.

examQuestions.question: Describe how to build comma-separated roll numbers without a final comma.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Start with an empty StringBuilder. Before appending any roll after the first, append comma-space. Append the roll, then convert the builder to String at the end. Handle an empty range separately.
